1#_: (Siman 87 seif 1) Only by way of cooking. See Peri Chadash that roasting, iruy, and cold into hot are also d'oraisa; and see Yeshuot Yaakov chapter 3 (siman 45) that wrote regarding hot meat that touched hot cheese — one may say it is forbidden only d'rabbanan — see there. And Hagahot Shaarei Dura wrote at end of the book (general rule 30 siman 4) regarding a piece that was pickled in milk — forbidden to cook it, for until now it is pickling prohibition d'rabbanan and now one violates d'oraisa cooking prohibition — end; it appears that if it was already cooked in milk it is permitted to cook again. And see Pri Megadim in Mishbetzot Zahav (siman 105 seif 2).
2#_: (Shach s.k. 2) And so Mordechai chapter Ein Ma'amidin — see there that he brought proof from that which we say: why did they forbid gentile cheeses? Because they curdle them in nevelah stomach skin — and why is it not also forbidden for benefit because of basar b'chalav? If so, since it is only by way of pickling d'rabbanan it is not forbidden for benefit. And I have difficulty: in truth it is difficult — why did they mention the reason of curdling in nevelah stomach skin? Behold even in kosher stomach skin there is basar b'chalav; and Tosafot challenged this and resolved: since it is only basar b'chalav d'rabbanan we are not concerned for uncertainty — and so for R' Yitzchak of Minash and Rambam — in truth there is sixty in the milk and its prohibition is only curdling agent, and through curdling agent basar b'chalav is not created; and since Mordechai does not hold these resolutions, Tosafot's question remains — why mention nevelah, behold even in kosher it is forbidden because of basar b'chalav; requires study. I also have difficulty on Mordechai's resolution that gentile cheeses were not forbidden for benefit — pickling is permitted for benefit; and so for Tosafot regarding benefit it is rabbinic uncertainty; nevertheless the question remains: gentile cheeses should be forbidden to make a dish from them — if the gentile curdled in skin and taste of meat in milk was absorbed by pickling, when he now cooks what was absorbed in the milk it is now cooking and he violates cooking basar b'chalav, and when he cooks it should be forbidden for benefit; requires study.
3#_: (In the hagahah) Permitted for benefit. And that he did not write permitted in cooking — this is because Beit Av considers it through pickling and salting; in this, cooking is forbidden since pickling and salting absorb milk in it, and when he cooks he now cooks meat with milk inside it and violates cooking, and it also becomes forbidden for benefit because d'oraisa basar b'chalav was created; investigate. And to cause thus — to mix meat in milk for benefit — see in Menachot general rule 5 s.k. 9.
4#_: (Taz s.k. 2) And in Derishah, etc. — and now one violates cooking prohibition — end.
5#_: (Shach small seif 5) Again came to hand the book Be'er Sheva. And see in his book Tzeda LaDerech parashat Tzav.
6#_: (Taz s.k. 4) Like woman's milk. This is astonishing — behold with woman's milk even b'dieved it is forbidden and is permitted only if it fell into a dish that is not recognizable; also per this proof it would be proven that with domestic animal meat too they do not forbid eating it; and so what Taz wrote, and so Rama's wording implies — one may place, etc.
7#_: (Seif 4) And if it fell into the dish. And if one mixed intentionally into the dish — forbidden to him and to one for whom it was done — see above (siman 66 in Shach s.k. 11).
8#_: (There in the hagahah) Or impure meat. I have difficulty — why forbid also impure meat in impure milk because of marit ayin?
9#_: (Shach s.k. 6) But because of marit ayin it does not deal. And so I found explicitly in responsum Tolodot Adam of Rashba (siman 200).
10#_: (Be'er Sheva) That one may cook for medical need. I have difficulty — nevertheless why permitted for benefit? Let us be concerned for marit ayin; requires study.
11#_: (Seif 6) One who cooks meat in milk-water. I have difficulty — what he wrote regarding wild animal and fowl that they are permitted in cooking and benefit since it is d'rabbanan — the same for milk-water; and I saw in Tiferet Lemoshe that he distinguishes — these here are from species of pure domestic animal forbidden d'oraisa and nevertheless, etc. Nevertheless I have difficulty — where do we find thus? From the thief who fell into mustard and fish that rose in a bowl of meat that it is permitted to eat in kutach because noten taam bar noten taam — although kutach is in milk-water, and this is Tosafot's proof from this — it is proven only for eating forbidden but not for cooking; and if from wording "one who cooks in milk-water is exempt" — it implies exempt but forbidden, as Rosh wrote — one may say as we explain "all meat is forbidden to cook" — meaning to eat; so too "one who cooks in milk-water" means one who eats [and conversely this resolves the sugya more — see full text in source]. Requires study; especially difficult regarding blood in milk — why did Chazal decree because of basar b'chalav? Behold otherwise not because of blood, etc.
